paragraphs: Rabbi Yaakov. (Without further designation; he is Rabbi Yaakov ben Korshai, a Tanna mentioned in the Mishnah.) Hyman presents the accepted identification that Rabbi Yaakov without further designation is the one sometimes called Rabbi Yaakov Korshai, or ben Korshai, or Kodshai (identified as Elisha–Acher’s daughter’s son, an identification Hyman challenges below). The proof of this is that in [Pirkei Avot 4:16-17](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.4.16-17): “Rabbi Yaakov says: This world is like a vestibule before the world to come; prepare yourself

in the vestibule so that you may enter the banquet hall. He used to say: Better one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the world to come.” This saying is cited in [Kohelet Rabbah 4:6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.4.6.1) and at the beginning of [Vayikra Rabbah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.3.1): “Rabbi Yaakov bar Korshai said: Better a handful of quiet in the world to come than two handfuls of toil and striving after wind in this world. He used to say: Better one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the world to come,

for the world to come comes only by virtue of this world.” This Rabbi Yaakov was the Tanna in the Sanhedrin of Usha, as stated explicitly in [Horayot 13b:13-15](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.13b.13-15): when Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Natan formed a conspiracy between them to remove Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel from his patriarchate, they decided to ask him to teach tractate Uktzin, knowing that he was not expert in it, and through this they would bring their plan from potential to actuality. When Rabbi Yaakov ben Karshai heard (Dikdukei Soferim reads ben

Kodshai)[^5], he said: “Perhaps, Heaven forbid, the matter will come to shame” (for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel). He went and sat behind Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s upper chamber, expounded, recited and repeated it; Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel understood his intent, paid attention and learned it, and through this he was saved from the upheaval. As for his teachers, we find only that he spoke in the name of Rabbi Meir, as in [Yevamot 102a:9-10](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.102a.9-10), [Gittin 14b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.14b.12) and [Bava Metzia 78b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.78b.6); but we find him as a colleague of the colleagues of

Rabbi Meir: he disagrees with Rabbi Yose, as in [Nedarim 12b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.12b.8); with Rabbi Natan, in Kiddushin 79a; with Rabbi Shimon, as in [Shabbat 144b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.144b.9) (and this is from [Tosefta Tahorot 10:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Tahorot.10.1)), [Kiddushin 57a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.57a.10) (from [Tosefta Negaim 8:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Negaim.8.8)), and [Bava Kamma 65a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.65a.11).[^6] Hyman reports that [Kiddushin 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.39b.7) and [the end of Chullin](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.142a.3) give the teaching in the name of Rabbi Yaakov’s school. He proposes attributing it directly to Rabbi Yaakov, citing [Tosefta Chullin, end of chapter 10](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Chullin.10.3) and Dikdukei Soferim.[^4] Here is the teaching:

“There is no mitzvah in the Torah whose reward is stated beside it on which the resurrection of the dead does not depend … Rav Yosef said: Had Acher (Elisha) expounded this verse like Rabbi Yaakov, his daughter’s son, he would not have sinned.” Hyman asks how Rav Yosef knew that Rabbi Yaakov was Acher’s daughter’s son — something we do not find anywhere. And even supposing that he had it as a tradition, is it not known that Rabbi

Yaakov was Rabbi’s teacher, as we will explain further? If so, how is it possible to say that when Elisha’s daughters came to take charity from Rabbi, Rabbi decreed and said, “Let there be none to extend kindness to him, and none to be gracious to his orphans,” as cited in [Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Chagigah.2.1.10)? Likewise in [Chagigah 15b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.15b.5), when Acher’s daughter came to Rabbi for support, he said to her, “Is there still of his seed in the world?” How could he say such a thing if his holy teacher

was this man’s daughter’s son? In truth, in [Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Chagigah.2.1.10), Rav Yosef’s saying is cited in other language, for they said there: “And he (Acher) did not know that Rabbi Yaakov had expounded it before him, ‘that it may go well with you,’” etc.; the plain sense is that Rabbi Yaakov had already expounded this.[^7] Likewise the words “his daughter’s son” are absent in Dikdukei Soferim on Chullin there. Hyman considers the truth clear: Rabbi Yaakov was never

Acher’s daughter’s son; he proposes that Kiddushin and Chullin there originally read that Rav Yosef said, “Had Acher expounded this verse like Rabbi Yaakov bar Karshai,” and from the word Karshai it became corrupted into ‘berateih’ (his daughter’s son); and with this everything comes to its place in peace. Let us return to our subject. He was the Tanna in the Sanhedrin of Usha, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel entrusted his precious son to him

to study mishnayot and baraitot with him (for this was Rabbi Yaakov’s appointment, for he was expert by heart in all the mishnayot and baraitot). This is stated in [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.10.5.2) and [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 10:1:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.10.1.3): Rabbi Yaakov ben Korshai was Rabbi’s teacher (but the reasoning of the mishnayot and their analysis Rabbi received from his father, from Rabbi Shimon and from his other teachers; only the correct readings did he receive from Rabbi Yaakov, as explained at length in his entry).[^8] For example:

In [Yoma 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.61a.12-15), Rabbi reports what Rabbi Yaakov taught him about the logs; in Gittin 14a, “Rabbi said in the name of Rabbi Yaakov”;[^9] in [Ketubot 7a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.7a.10) he disagrees with him, but Rabbi conceded like Rabbi Yaakov; likewise in [Chullin 45b:10-11](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.45b.10-11) he disagrees with him, and Rabbi ruled like Rabbi Yaakov. We find that he disagrees with Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah, as in [Sukkah 4b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.4b.6) and [Sukkah 26b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.26b.1) and [Beitzah 35b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.35b.1). Of those who speak in his name (besides Rabbi) we find:

Elazar ben Yehudah of Kefar Avelim, as in [Zevachim 28a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.28a.12). Yehudah ben Nekisa in his name, as in [Chullin 118b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.118b.22). In [Chullin 98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.98a.9), Rabbi Nachum cites Rabbi Biryim, who reports the teaching in the name of an elder named Rabbi Yaakov.[^3] Well known to all is what they said in [Bava Kamma 39b:8-9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.39b.8-9): “A deaf-mute’s ox, an imbecile’s or a minor’s, that gored — Rabbi Yaakov pays half damages,” and they ask, “What has Rabbi Yaakov to do with it?”

He is likewise mentioned in [Shevuot 3b:12-13](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.3b.12-13), holding that one is not flogged for a prohibition involving no action, and disagreeing with Rabbi Yehudah. In [Menachot 36a:8-9](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.36a.8-9) he disagrees with the sages and holds that one wears tefillin until the foot traffic ends from the market. In Bekhorot 7a he holds that the honey of gazin and hornets is forbidden.[^10] In [Bereshit Rabbah 17:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.17.2), he said: “Whoever has no wife
lives without good, without help, without joy, without blessing, without atonement.”

notes.text: This notice is scan-derived, with sentences continuing between L-groups; their source portions and complete sequence remain intact. The opening conventional claim that Yaakov is Acher’s daughter’s son is intentionally followed by Hyman’s rejection and proposed קרשי→ברתיה corruption; the English attributes this argument and does not admit or merge a genealogy. ח״ש is interpreted as חס ושלום. TEVayikra3:1 has Yaakov bar Korshoi, supporting bar rather than an invented RabbiKorshai. NamedDavidsonBK39b asks what Yaakov has to do with paying and then emends to Yaakov says: he pays; the English deliberately preserves Yaakov pays so the objection remains intelligible. The supplied Gittin14a and14b locators are retained; the saved14b paragraph contains RabbiYehudahHaNasi reportingYaakov reportingMeir. The saved14a opening scalar is merely a bounded nonmatch, not a whole-folio absence claim. GuggenheimerJTChag2:1’s bounded connected Acher/Yaakov/daughters passage was read, not the entire long scalar; it gives Yaakov’s prior exposition without establishing Hyman’s proposed scribal history. His correct-readings-only teacher distinction and chronological arguments remain his account.

The consulted Vayikra Rabbah has Yaakov bar Korshoi, not an independently attested Rabbi Korshai. Bava Kamma 39b first prints Yaakov pays and then objects and emends it to Yaakov says; both steps explain the supplied quotation. The whole consulted Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1 scalar has now been read, including Yaakov’s prior interpretation and the daughters’ request for support; the current note truthfully recording an earlier bounded read is retained verbatim. These witnesses do not establish Hyman’s proposed קרשי-to-ברתיה copying history or admit or reject a genealogy on independent authority. His categorical rejection, accepted-identification framing and correct-readings-only teacher distinction remain attributed with their original force, and all scan-unit continuations remain intact.

[Chullin 98a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.98a.9) places Rabbi Nachum and Rabbi Biryim at the end of a longer chain that begins with Rav Shemen bar Abba. [Chullin 118b:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.118b.22) has Yehudah ben Nekosa citing Rabbi Yaakov. [Yoma 61a:12–15](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.61a.12-15) first says Rabbi Yaakov “made a distinction for me” and then proposes “taught me” after raising an objection.

The Hebrew in the consulted [Kiddushin 39b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.39b.7) and [Chullin 142a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.142a.3) attributes the teaching directly to Rabbi Yaakov, as does [Tosefta Chullin 10:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Chullin.10.3). The Davidson English of Chullin still introduces the teaching through Rabbi Yaakov’s school.

In [Horayot 13b:13-15](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.13b.13-15), the consulted Hebrew reads “ben Kodshai,” and the English renders the name “ben Korshei.” [Kohelet Rabbah 4:6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.4.6.1) has Yaakov berabbi Korshai, while [Vayikra Rabbah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.3.1) has Yaakov bar Korshoi. [Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2083&lang=en) records both Korshai and ben Korshai and recounts the same Uktzin episode.

The consulted text of [Nedarim 12b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.12b.8) names Rabbi Yehudah in disagreement with Rabbi Yaakov. Hyman gives Rabbi Yose. The disagreement with Rabbi Natan appears at [Kiddushin 79b:2-3](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.79b.2-3). Hyman gives 79a. [Shabbat 144b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.144b.9) gives Rabbi Yaakov’s position about olive discharge, and [Tosefta Tahorot 10:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Tahorot.10.1) also gives Rabbi Shimon’s position. The consulted [Tosefta Negaim 8:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Negaim.8.8) gives Rabbi Yaakov the permissive ruling and Rabbi Shimon the prohibitive one, the reverse of their rulings in [Kiddushin 57a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.57a.10). Rabbi Yaakov’s ruling at [Bava Kamma 65a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.65a.11) is followed by Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s position on [Bava Kamma 65b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.65b.1).

The narrator of [Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Chagigah.2.1.10) reports Rabbi Yaakov’s earlier interpretation without naming Rav Yosef as the speaker. The passage also recounts the daughters’ appeal for support. Hyman draws his conclusion about the proposed relationship from comparing the accounts.

[Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.10.5.2) and [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 10:1:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.10.1.3) both describe Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi as Yaakov’s student. The consulted Hebrew gives bar Kodshai in Shabbat and bar Korshai in Pesachim. Hyman draws the distinction between learning the correct readings and learning their interpretation.

The chain “Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi in the name of Rabbi Yaakov, who spoke in the name of Rabbi Meir” is in [Gittin 14b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.14b.12). The two Sukkah passages, [Sukkah 4b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.4b.6) and [Sukkah 26b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.26b.1), name the Sages in disagreement with Rabbi Yaakov. [Beitzah 35b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.35b.1) explicitly names Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah.
The baraita giving Rabbi Yaakov’s ruling on the honey of gazin and hornets appears at [Bekhorot 7b:6-9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.7b.6-9). Hyman gives 7a.
